reviewed: On the Quanta 40, jumper J7 selects the boot ROM source.
reword: Jumper J7 on the Quanta 40 selects the source of the boot ROM.
different: On the Quanta 40, jumper J9 enables the serial console at 9600 baud.

reviewed: A single 80mm fan cools the CPU heatsink on the Quanta 40.
reword: The Quanta 40's CPU heatsink is cooled by a single 80mm fan.
different: The fan connector on the Quanta 40 supplies 5 volts and a tachometer signal.

reviewed: The Quanta 40 uses electrolytic capacitors, not solid polymer, on the power rail.
reword: On the Quanta 40, the power rail uses electrolytic capacitors rather than solid polymer.
different: Capacitor C14 near the VRM occasionally bulges after decades of thermal cycling.

reviewed: The boot ROM on the Quanta 40 runs before any RAM is initialized.
reword: Before any RAM initializes, the Quanta 40's boot ROM runs first.
different: The boot ROM on the Quanta 40 is socketed for field replacement.

reviewed: The Quanta 40's SCSI bus requires termination on both end devices.
reword: Termination on both end devices is required by the Quanta 40's SCSI bus.
different: A loose SCSI terminator on the Quanta 40 causes spurious bus errors.

reviewed: Four SIMM slots on the Quanta 40 accept up to 64 megabytes.
reword: The Quanta 40's four SIMM slots accept up to 64 megabytes of RAM.
different: RAM slot 2 on the Quanta 40 is disabled when the math coprocessor is fitted.

reviewed: The Quanta 40's power supply delivers +5, +12, and -12 volts.
reword: +5, +12, and -12 volts are delivered by the Quanta 40's power supply.
different: The PSU fan on the Quanta 40 fails after roughly ten thousand hours.

reviewed: The Quanta 40 keyboard uses a round DIN connector with six pins.
reword: A round six-pin DIN connector is used by the Quanta 40 keyboard.
different: The keyboard connector on the Quanta 40 also carries a clock signal.

reviewed: The Quanta 40 monitor output uses separate horizontal and vertical sync signals.
reword: Separate horizontal and vertical sync signals are used by the Quanta 40's monitor output.
different: The monitor sync on the Quanta 40 accepts only negative-going pulses.

reviewed: A CR2032 battery backs the NVRAM on the Quanta 40 for ten years.
reword: The Quanta 40's NVRAM is backed by a CR2032 battery for ten years.
different: The NVRAM battery socket on the Quanta 40 corrodes if left drained.

reviewed: The Quanta 40 ships with a single 3.5-inch floppy drive at drive 0.
reword: Drive 0 on the Quanta 40 is a single 3.5-inch floppy drive.
different: The floppy drive on the Quanta 40 reads 1.44-megabyte disks natively.

reviewed: The Quanta 40 firmware lives in an EPROM under socket U12.
reword: Socket U12 on the Quanta 40 holds the firmware EPROM.
different: The Quanta 40 firmware checks the RAM count at every power-on self-test.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 tape drive records at 800 bits per inch on the main track.
reword: On the Kestrel 3000 tape drive, the main track records at 800 bits per inch.
different: The Kestrel 3000 tape drive advances the tape at 12 inches per second.

reviewed: Each Kestrel 3000 cassette holds 4.6 megabytes of user data when packed tightly.
reword: When packed tightly, each Kestrel 3000 cassette holds 4.6 megabytes of user data.
different: The Kestrel 3000 cassette uses a quarter-inch wide magnetic tape reel.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 features four independent read-write heads on its head carriage.
reword: Four independent read-write heads sit on the head carriage of the Kestrel 3000.
different: The Kestrel 3000 head carriage steps in 200 steps per inch.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 accepts a half-height cassette cartridge with a metal-particle coating.
reword: A half-height cassette cartridge with metal-particle coating is accepted by the Kestrel 3000.
different: The Kestrel 3000 cartridge door latches with a soft-close spring mechanism.

reviewed: A stepper motor drives the Kestrel 3000 tape transport at a constant 300 RPM.
reword: At a constant 300 RPM, a stepper motor drives the Kestrel 3000 tape transport.
different: The Kestrel 3000 transport belt is made of braided Teflon fiber.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 includes a 16-kilobyte FIFO buffer before data reaches the host.
reword: Before data reaches the host, the Kestrel 3000 includes a 16-kilobyte FIFO buffer.
different: The Kestrel 3000 buffer uses static RAM retained by a coin cell battery.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 applies Reed-Solomon error correction to every written data block.
reword: Every data block the Kestrel 3000 writes gets Reed-Solomon error correction.
different: The Kestrel 3000 reports a CRC mismatch on the first 64 bytes.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 connects to the host via a 44-pin ribbon cable.
reword: A 44-pin ribbon cable connects the Kestrel 3000 to the host computer.
different: The Kestrel 3000 host interface runs at a 2 megabyte-per-second transfer rate.

reviewed: A green activity LED on the Kestrel 3000 lights during read and write.
reword: During read and write, a green activity LED lights on the Kestrel 3000.
different: A red error LED on the Kestrel 3000 signals a tape end condition.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 tape drive requires a stable +12 volt DC supply rail.
reword: A stable +12 volt DC supply rail is required by the Kestrel 3000 tape drive.
different: The Kestrel 3000 draws a peak of 2.4 amps during motor start-up.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 uses Modified Frequency Modulation encoding on the tape surface.
reword: Modified Frequency Modulation encoding is used by the Kestrel 3000 on the tape surface.
different: The Kestrel 3000 servo track maintains tape azimuth alignment at 5 degrees.

reviewed: The Kestrel 3000 rewinds a full cassette in under twelve seconds.
reword: A full cassette is rewound by the Kestrel 3000 in under twelve seconds.
different: The Kestrel 3000 auto-reverses between the A and B sides of the tape.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 uses the Yamaha YM2612 for FM synthesis.
reword: FM synthesis on the Vireo 9 is handled by the Yamaha YM2612.
different: The Vireo 9 uses the Cirrus Logic LR35512 for PCM playback.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 defaults to IRQ 5 for its primary sound channel.
reword: IRQ 5 is the default for the Vireo 9's primary sound channel.
different: The Vireo 9 can be jumpered to IRQ 10 for MIDI.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 assigns DMA channel 1 for sample playback.
reword: DMA channel 1 is assigned by the Vireo 9 for sample playback.
different: The Vireo 9 uses DMA channel 5 for cartridge audio input.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 exposes a 25-pin DB connector for expansion.
reword: A 25-pin DB connector on the Vireo 9 is used for expansion.
different: The Vireo 9 features a 9-pin DIN connector for MIDI output.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 mixer provides four independent audio output channels.
reword: Four independent audio output channels are provided by the Vireo 9 mixer.
different: The Vireo 9 mixer includes a dedicated reverb effect bus.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 synth engine supports up to eight simultaneous voices.
reword: Up to eight simultaneous voices are supported by the Vireo 9 synth engine.
different: The Vireo 9 synth engine offers sixteen programmable oscillator patches.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 accepts a proprietary ROM cartridge for sound libraries.
reword: Sound libraries on the Vireo 9 are loaded via a proprietary ROM cartridge.
different: The Vireo 9 cartridge slot also provides direct MIDI sequencing access.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 clock runs at 4.43 MHz for audio sync.
reword: Audio sync on the Vireo 9 uses a 4.43 MHz clock.
different: The Vireo 9 clock can be overclocked to 7.16 MHz.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 draws power from the bus's +5V rail.
reword: The +5V rail of the bus powers the Vireo 9.
different: The Vireo 9 also uses the bus's -12V rail for analog filters.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 volume knob is a 10k ohm potentiometer.
reword: A 10k ohm potentiometer serves as the Vireo 9 volume knob.
different: The Vireo 9 has a separate balance control for stereo output.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 DSP handles hardware reverb and echo effects.
reword: Hardware reverb and echo effects on the Vireo 9 are handled by its DSP.
different: The Vireo 9 DSP also converts digital audio to 16-bit resolution.

reviewed: The Vireo 9 retains presets using a CR2032 backup battery.
reword: A CR2032 backup battery lets the Vireo 9 retain its presets.
different: The Vireo 9 battery housing is located beneath the main PCB.
